purpose: Close ASVS V11.1.3 with a repository-owned mechanism that enumerates every cryptographic instance rather than only the insecure ones, and correct the V11.4.1 note it immediately proved incomplete.
requiredInvariants: The mechanism enumerates instances; it never judges them, so a clean run is not a security claim.
An operation with no sites is reported as zero, never omitted.
Key material is named and never read; no key value can reach the artefact.
A pattern match that is configuration rather than key material is labelled, never silently dropped.
The artefact is committed and a test fails when it goes stale, so the inventory is maintained rather than a snapshot.
The artefact states its own limits, including that it is not a key-management policy.
A finding that contradicts an already-merged note corrects that note in place.
No security gate is weakened and no action reference is added; the pinning ratchet stays at 1028.
No product logic, production, REG.RU, DNS or database change.
acceptance: The scanner covers all 17 operation classes and records the algorithm for each, not just the call.
A test proves a key value in source cannot appear in the artefact.
The staleness guard was mutation-checked: editing the committed inventory turns it red.
V11.1.3 moves FAIL to PASS with conditions watching the script, the artefact, the staleness guard and the CI wiring.
V11.4.1 keeps PASS and its note is corrected to name the two TOTP HMAC-SHA1 sites and why they are approved.
V11.1.1, V11.1.2 and V11.1.4 stay FAIL, because policy is not a measurement.
The evidence gate rejects 0 decisions and all 60 security-script tests pass.
